goal.problem: Scribe uses a monolithic notes.jsonl for all note storage, which grows unbounded, risks line-level corruption, and forces full-file parsing for every operation.
goal.solution: Create a new scribe/store.py storage engine module implementing a folder-per-type layout with per-folder index.jsonl files, individual .md note files, and a global auto-increment counter.
goal.value: Provides the foundational storage layer that all subsequent scribe v2 work (CLI rewrite, migration, startup) builds on, with isolation between note types and single-file granularity.

components.name: ScribeStore class
components.description: Main interface. Initialized with a state_dir (Path). Provides methods for all CRUD operations on notes and learnings. Manages the folder layout, index I/O, and file operations.

components.name: Index I/O helpers
components.description: read_index(type_dir) -> list[dict], write_index(type_dir, entries), append_index(type_dir, entry). Each reads/writes a per-folder index.jsonl. Uses FileLock for concurrent safety.

components.name: Global counter
components.description: next_id file at state_dir/next_id holding a single integer. read_next_id() -> int, increment_id() -> int (atomic read-increment-write). Falls back to scanning all indexes for max ID if file is missing.

components.name: Note file helpers
components.description: write_note_file(type_dir, id, content), read_note_file(type_dir, id) -> str | None. Pure content in .md files, no frontmatter.

components.name: Layout initialization
components.description: ensure_layout(state_dir) creates all type folders, archive subfolders, and next_id file if they don't exist.

shape.integration_point: scribe/store.py — new module, no integration with existing code yet. Phase 2 wires notes.py to use it.
shape.pattern: Similar to the existing memory/ file-per-entry pattern but adds index files for fast listing.
shape.data_flow: Caller -> ScribeStore method -> read/write index.jsonl + individual .md file -> return result.
shape.dependencies: core/utils/filelock.py for index writes. pathlib, json (stdlib).

behavior.input: Method calls with note type, content, session_id, optional metadata.
behavior.processing: 1. ensure_layout() creates folder structure on first use. 2. add_note(type, content, session_id, ...) reads next_id, increments, writes index entry, writes .md file. 3. get_note(id) scans type indexes for matching ID, reads .md file. 4. list_notes(type=None, status='active', search=None) reads index(es), filters, sorts by timestamp. 5. update_note(id, **kwargs) finds and updates index entry. 6. archive_note(id) moves index entry to archive/index.jsonl, moves .md to archive/. 7. Learning methods follow same pattern in learnings/ folder.
behavior.output: Dicts for single notes, lists of dicts for queries. Each dict has: id, type, status, session, timestamp, summary, has_body.

error_cases.trigger: Type folder or index doesn't exist
error_cases.behavior: Create it on the fly via ensure_layout().

error_cases.trigger: Note .md file missing but index entry exists
error_cases.behavior: Return the index entry with content=None and a warning flag.
Scan all indexes for max ID, recreate counter.
Skip the entry, log to stderr.

edge_cases.behavior: Search archive indexes, return with status='archived'.
FileLock on next_id file and on type index file ensures atomicity.
Write empty .md file, summary in index is empty string.

in_scope: ScribeStore class with full CRUD for notes and learnings
Global next_id counter with fallback rebuild
out_of_scope: CLI argument parsing — that stays in notes.py, rewired in Phase 2
Migration from old JSONL layout — Phase 3
Auto-archive timer logic — Phase 2 will wire the existing 30-day logic to use store methods
must_not_break: No changes to existing scribe/notes.py — this is a new module only
No changes to any other existing files

acceptance_criteria: Given a fresh state_dir, when ensure_layout() is called, then all type folders (todos, handoffs, decisions, wishlists, blockers, context, general, learnings) exist with empty index.jsonl and archive/ subfolders
Given an empty store, when add_note(type='todo', content='fix bug', session='abc123') is called, then next_id increments, todos/index.jsonl has one entry with id=1, and todos/1.md contains 'fix bug'
Given notes of multiple types exist, when list_notes() is called with no type filter, then all notes are returned sorted by timestamp descending
Given a note with id=5 of type 'todo', when get_note(5) is called, then the index metadata and .md content are both returned
Given a note with id=5, when archive_note(5) is called, then the index entry moves to todos/archive/index.jsonl and 5.md moves to todos/archive/5.md
Given two concurrent add_note calls, when both complete, then both entries have unique IDs and both index entries and .md files exist without corruption
Given next_id file is deleted, when add_note is called, then the counter is rebuilt from max ID across all indexes and the new note gets the correct next ID
Given a malformed line in an index.jsonl, when list_notes is called, then the bad line is skipped with a warning and all valid entries are returned
